articles.title: Carbon 3K Fine
articles.summary: Dark charcoal 3K carbon twill weave, tight diagonal pattern, glossy clearcoat, subtle sparkle. Reads as dark charcoal carbon-fibre weave, a fine chevron texture that turns to a dark gloss grey-black with faint diagonal grain.
articles.what: Tight high-frequency 3K ±45° twill — small aerospace weave with crisp fiber striation under gloss clear Up close: Tight rows of short rectangular tow blocks, each a few pixels wide, alternating diagonal direction in a zigzag herringbone, in dark charcoal-black with slightly lighter tops and dark gaps. Low contrast; the blocks are rounded and softly lit. From a distance: Reads as dark charcoal carbon-fibre weave, a fine chevron texture that turns to a dark gloss grey-black with faint diagonal grain. Measured spec (average): metal 109, roughness 42, coat 16. Shine: high gloss. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.

how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Carbon 3K Fine on the hood".
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, spoiler and mirrors: classic carbon locations
Side skirts and lower body for trim accents
White, yellow or red numbers read well; dark numbers vanish and thin ones get chopped up by the weave.
Red, white or neon stripes and block graphics: classic carbon-and-colour racing look
Pairs well with: red, white, chrome, gold.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not Carbon Fibre with a large weave: this one is tight and fine, so it reads as texture from afar
Not satin black: it is a glossy clear-coated weave
Avoid: dark numbers over the weave, next to other busy dark textures.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 109 (pearl-level metal), roughness 42 (high gloss), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: dark numbers over the weave, next to other busy dark textures.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: red, white or neon stripes and block graphics: classic carbon-and-colour racing look; chrome or gold pinstripes and edge lines: premium trim
Patterns to avoid: other weave, mesh or hex patterns: textures clash; dark camo or graphics: vanish into the base
Spec overlays that work: gloss/matte stripe bands: matte sections on glossy carbon; fine sparkle spec: adds glint along the tows
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
